title: InvokeEnvelope
description: Request/response envelope for tool invocation between the app (client) and botd (server) over the @multibot abstract-namespace Unix socket. Frames are newline-delimited JSON. One of Request or Response per frame.

tool.description: Tool id to invoke, e.g. "shell.run" (see builtin-tools-phase1.json).

args.description: Tool arguments. Validated by botd against the target ToolDescriptor's input_schema.

ctx.description: Invocation context, assigned by the caller and echoed back on the response.

session.description: Session id (sessions.db row) in which the invocation occurs.

turn.description: Zero-based turn index within the session.

corr_id.description: Correlation id (UUIDv7). Echoed verbatim in the response; used by the client to match pending invocations.

priority.description: Scheduling priority for the invocation on the botd side (queue ordering, not a risk control).

Response.description: Server → client invocation result. Exactly one response per corr_id; blocked invocations (needs_approval) resolve to a single terminal response after the human verdict.

corr_id.description: Echoed correlation id from the request.

status.description: ok = executed; error = execution failed; needs_approval = blocked pending a human verdict (terminal response delivered after the verdict, carrying the outcome).

result.description: Tool result payload. Shape is tool-specific; present on ok. Omitted on error and on needs_approval.

message.description: Human-readable detail. Never contains secret values.

trace.description: Execution trace. Present on ok; informational on error.

backend.description: Backend actually used, e.g. "termux". Null-equivalent when execution was blocked before backend resolution.

approval_ref.description: Approval record id (audit). Present when an approval was required or when the call was a standing-grant re-use.

side_effects.description: Declared side effects of the invocation, for trace chips and the audit log.

files_touched.description: Filesystem paths read or written during the invocation.

bus_events.description: Bus events emitted during the invocation, e.g. "cron_result", "task_completed".
